speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Neck (Secondary to Colon Cancer)

I have reached my conclusion based on the patient's age, the location of the swelling on the nape of the neck, the cystic nature of the lesion, and specifically the history of colon cancer, which suggests a potential metastatic deposit in the cervical lymph nodes. The lack of fever, pain, or constitutional symptoms further supports a chronic, likely malignant process rather than an acute infectious etiology.
